part: children's health details handled through the cloud model (CRT-10 and CRT-13)
where: CRT-10 caveats; CRT-13 caveats and safety
problem: Both cards send a child's health details (which medicine was given and when, allergies, medicines, conditions) to OpenAI and treat that as acceptable, with a tip to use a nickname. Tony has never said this is acceptable, and the catalog's own summary says store:false still leaves up to 30 days of provider logs and recommends keeping medical bills away from the model until Zero Data Retention is approved.
checked: owner-facts.md (no decision on children's health data; only the Zero Data Retention application is agreed). Roadmap line 20 ('Private data arrives only after local models and egress controls are in place') and section 9, which has no row on this. frame.json findings ('store:false protects less than the plan assumed') and its attachments decision ('no medical bills until approval'). CRT-10 caveat 3, CRT-13 caveat 5 and its safety text.

proposal.text: Question: 'May Happy handle your children's health details (doses given, allergies, medicines, conditions) through the OpenAI model before Zero Data Retention is approved?' Default if no answer: no. The dose log (CRT-10) and the medical sections of the CRT-13 pages wait for the approval or for a local model; until then the sitter sheet and the form answers leave the medical section blank for a parent to fill in by hand.

loses: The dose log and the pre-filled medical sections until Zero Data Retention is approved or a local model exists.

Only school is known; none of the rest has been said by Tony or is recorded in the config repo.
checked: owner-facts.md (grandparents, a sitter, activities and the number of children are all in the never-stated list). family.json5 (two adults and nothing else). The card's sources: Ready.gov, the paediatricians' sitter checklist and the CDC records page describe households in general, not this one.

proposal.text: Question: 'Which of these would you use: (a) a one-page emergency plan to print, (b) a sheet to hand to a sitter or grandparent, (c) a checklist and paste-ready answers for camp or sports forms?' Default if no answer: build (a) and the fixed emergency reply only; (b) and (c) are added when you name a carer or a form. Reword the example so it gives no count of children.

loses: The sitter sheet and the form kit until Tony asks for them.

part: both parents text Happy at every dose
problem: The card's value rests on both parents texting Happy each time they give medicine. Nobody has said they would, Jordan has not been asked, and the card's own caveats say a shared note on the phones or a paper log kept with the medicine does the same job and still works when Happy is down.
checked: owner-facts.md (medications and 'whether Jordan wants any of this' are in the never-stated list; value and wave are agent-assigned). The card's poison centre source, which recommends a log kept with the medicine. The card's own Apple Notes caveat (caveat 4) and caveat 5.

proposal.text: Question: 'When a child is ill, would you and Jordan text Happy each dose, or keep using a shared note or paper by the bottle?' Default if no answer: take CRT-10 out of wave B and park it until one of you asks. The absence-note wording and a check-in reminder already work as ordinary chat and a timed reminder (F007).

loses: The 'last dose logged' answer with its elapsed time worked out in code.

part: 'the time comes from the message timestamp' and 'computed in code'
problem: The card says the dose time is taken from the message's own timestamp and worked out in code. Nothing on the card shows that the log tool can see when a text was sent, and when a parent writes 'at 7:40' it is the model that turns that into a clock time. So the one number the card says must not be wrong still depends on the model.
checked: The card's sources (tool-plugins.md and the scheduler page say nothing about message time). The installed tool-context type (dist/agent-harness-runtime-BbN1SctJ.d.ts:22991), which gives a tool the trusted sender id but no message time; read, not run.

proposal.text: Reword to: 'The log time is the Mac's clock when the log tool runs, unless the parent states a time. A stated time ("at 7:40") is read by the model, so Happy's confirmation spells it out in full, with the day and morning or evening, and the parent corrects it if wrong. Only the subtraction is done in code.' Add one test before go-live: a dose texted with a stated time just after midnight and one late in the evening.

proposal.text: Question: 'Which of these do you have and want a monthly heads-up for: adult passports, children's passports, driving licences, a car (inspection, registration, oil change), a domain name, Global Entry, a furnace filter, a yearly check-up per child, policy or warranty end dates, tax or benefit dates, gift dates?' loses: Row types Tony does not confirm are not built until he names them.

loses: If G001 is built later, a short-notice row could be missed in a month when a cap or mute is active, until the check is added.

part: daily checks run from OpenClaw's own scheduler and reach Tony as an iMessage text
problem: Tony's recorded decision is that alerts come by ntfy from the one Grafana screen, and the host checks that exist today run from launchd and feed that screen. The card instead runs the new checks inside OpenClaw's scheduler and texts the result over iMessage, without saying why. A text cannot report a broken iMessage channel, and the card itself says the audit has never been run from the scheduler.
checked: owner-facts.md ('One Grafana screen; alerts by ntfy; healthchecks.io for silence'). Roadmap line 447. Config repo: observability/grafana/provisioning/alerting/contact-points.yaml has the ntfy contact point, bin/happy-sandbox-check is a launchd job that pushes a 0-or-1 metric for a Grafana rule, and system/happy-inspect already holds the commands. G008 caveat 4 and unverified item 4.

proposal.text: Question: 'Should the daily sign-in and plugin check and the monthly audit result reach you through ntfy like the other alerts, or as a text from Happy?' Default if no answer: ntfy, built like the existing sandbox check (a launchd script that pushes one ok-or-not metric per check, plus a Grafana rule), with no OpenClaw scheduler job and no dependency on the jobs registry (G003).

loses: The finding's own wording in the alert: the ntfy alerts carry a rule name and summary only, so Tony reads the detail with happy-inspect.

problem: Tony decided that evals run on demand and after a critical-path change, never on a schedule. 'After each change' promises more runs than that, and each run calls the real model and costs tokens.

proposal.text: Replace 'also check Happy's behaviour after each change' with 'are there for Tony to run on demand and after a critical-path change, as already decided'.

part: 'sent 2 texts to Jordan' line taken from OpenClaw's message audit rows
problem: The review promises a count of texts sent to a named person and says it comes from OpenClaw's message audit rows. Those rows hold no readable recipient and are not tied to the asking parent's chat, so they cannot produce that line as written.
checked: Installed docs/gateway/audit.md, privacy model section (lines 404 to 425): target identifiers are kept only as keyed pseudonyms and message records leave out the session key. The card's own note on audit.md:21 ('it cannot say which list item or recipient'). G009's build note: sends go through the built-in message tool. The installed hook types (dist/hook-runner-global-FJPVxfg8.d.ts:1284): an after-tool hook is given the tool's parameters; read, not run.

proposal.text: Drop the `logging.audit.messages` dependency. Take the line from an observe-only `after_tool_call` hook on the `message` tool, the same kind of hook the card already plans for memory saves, which is given the target; or word the line without a name ('sent 2 texts for you').

part: 'undo that' for list items and calendar entries
problem: Undoing a list item or a calendar entry needs each item to keep one stable id, and needs Happy to tell whether a parent has edited it since. The card lists both as unknown because neither tool is installed, yet the description promises undo for lists and the calendar and does not say what happens if the ids do not hold.
checked: G006 unverified item 9 and caveat 3. F030's unverified list (writing to a shared list from the Mac is itself unproven). G006 caveat 5, the card's own view that undo mainly earns its place for household facts. The scheduler page on the card (managing-jobs.md:136): removing a timed reminder by id is documented.

proposal.text: Promise undo only for household facts and timed reminders at first. Once the Reminders bridge and the calendar write exist, add an item, let it sync to a phone, edit it there, and check that the id is unchanged and that the tool can see the edit; only then extend undo to lists and the calendar.

loses: Undo for list items and calendar entries until the test passes.
